title: Consistent bedtime
why: Most growth hormone is released during deep sleep, and regular sleep timing helps you get enough of it.
dailyTarget: Same bedtime and wake time (within 1 hour), every day

title: Get enough sleep
why: Teens generally need 8 to 10 hours; short sleep is linked to poorer health and disrupted growth-related hormone rhythms.

title: Screens off before bed
why: Bright screens late in the evening can delay sleep, making it harder to get enough deep sleep.
dailyTarget: No screens for 45 minutes before bed

title: Protein at every meal
why: Growing bodies need protein as a building material for bone and muscle.
dailyTarget: A palm-sized protein portion at 3 meals

title: Calcium-rich foods
why: Calcium is a key mineral for building strong bones during the teen years.

title: Vitamin D from sun and food
why: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium; ask a doctor before taking supplements.
dailyTarget: 15 minutes of daylight outdoors plus vitamin D foods

title: Fruit and vegetables
why: A varied diet supplies the vitamins and minerals that support normal growth.

title: Drink water
why: Good hydration supports energy, focus and recovery from activity.

title: Move every day
why: Regular physical activity supports healthy bones and overall development.
dailyTarget: 60 minutes of active play or sport

title: Weight-bearing play
why: Jumping, running and ball sports load the bones, which helps them become stronger.
dailyTarget: 20 minutes of jumping, running or ball games

title: Stretch and mobility
why: Gentle stretching keeps muscles flexible and helps you move comfortably.

title: Posture check-ins
why: Good posture lets you stand at your true height; it does not change how tall you will become.
dailyTarget: Stand tall against a wall for 1 minute, 3 times

title: Desk setup and breaks
why: Breaking up long sitting reduces stiffness and slouching.
dailyTarget: Stand and stretch every 45 minutes of sitting

title: Light, balanced backpack
why: A heavy bag carried on one shoulder can cause uneven posture and back discomfort.
dailyTarget: Use both straps; keep the bag under 10% of body weight
